claim_hierarchy.claim: Aggregate abundance and spatial structure need not recover together, and abundance direction does not uniquely determine spatial direction.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Used to reject sign-locking in the focal taxon; not presented as a novel general principle.

claim_hierarchy.claim: A severe Ross breeding-census collapse was followed by near-complete aggregate rebound that closely retraced the proportional inverse path of the preceding loss.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Spatial decomposition is post-result; counts do not identify individual returning birds; 9.41% mismatch is ordinary within Ross.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Persistent Adélie decline at Palmer and Signy departed from proportional thinning and concentrated breeding abundance among fewer effective units.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Identifies unequal attrition relative to fixed composition, not a single causal vital rate.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Beaufort growth after capacity release departed from proportional expansion, while independent evidence showed reduced export toward Ross Island.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Census and movement evidence are independent streams; no individual-level mediation is inferred.

claim_hierarchy.claim: The biological route of change may influence whether a previous multi-node breeding allocation remains recoverable, through effects on breeding expression, the site-affiliated demographic pool, or breeding capacity.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Only one clean temporary-shock baseline–trough–rebound system is available; process classes were formalized after outcomes were known.

common_inferential_principle: Compare observed local change with the proportional spatial allocation expected if aggregate change occurred without additional reorganization.
forbidden_promotions: aggregate-versus-spatial recovery decoupling is newly discovered here
process class significantly predicts one pooled spatial-reversibility effect size
short disturbances are reversible and long disturbances are irreversible
the same Ross individuals returned to the same breeding units
site fidelity caused the Ross inverse-path recovery
the current synthesis prospectively confirms a universal process-dependent spatial-memory law
